ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Endocrinology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Palpitations, heat intolerance, and unintentional weight loss

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She presents to the clinic with a 2-month history of palpitations, heat intolerance, and unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds despite an increased appetite.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- History of papillary thyroid carcinoma
- Postsurgical hypothyroidism

Her past medical history is significant for a total thyroidectomy 5 years ago due to papillary thyroid carcinoma.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection (5 years prior)
- Parathyroid autotransplantation

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Levothyroxine 112 mcg (1.6 mcg/kg) orally daily
- Calcium carbonate with vitamin D3 600 mg-400 IU orally twice daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of thyroid disease
- No family history of endocrine malignancies
- Mother with hypertension
- Father with type 2 diabetes mellitus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Marketing coordinator and part-time fitness instructor.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
She denies any changes in her bowel habits or hair texture.

VITAL SIGNS:
Heart rate is 102 bpm, blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, she has a fine tremor in her outstretched hands. There is no goiter or thyroid nodule palpable, and her thyroidectomy scar is well-healed without evidence of local recurrence.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory tests reveal the following:

- Serum thyroxine (T4): Elevated
- Serum triiodothyronine (T3): Elevated
- Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH): Suppressed
- Serum thyroglobulin: Undetectable

OTHER STUDIES:
- Radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU): Low

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. James Okafor, MD
Department: Endocrinology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Anxiety, excessive sweating, and mood changes (brought in by roommate)

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma and postsurgical hypothyroidism is returning for evaluation of symptoms similar to January 2020. The roommate notes she has become unusually preoccupied with fitness and has been following extreme dieting and exercise regimens. She reports weight loss of 8 pounds over the past 2 months despite a good appetite.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Thyrotoxicosis factitia (Exogenous thyroid hormone intake) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of papillary thyroid carcinoma
- Postsurgical hypothyroidism

She has no personal or family history of thyroid disease, and her last physical exam one year ago was normal.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection (5 years prior)
- Parathyroid autotransplantation

MEDICATIONS:
The patient admits to purchasing "metabolism boosters" online but denies using any prescription medications.

Home Medications:
- Levothyroxine 112 mcg (1.6 mcg/kg) orally daily
- Calcium carbonate with vitamin D3 600 mg-400 IU orally twice daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
She has no personal or family history of thyroid disease

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Marketing coordinator and part-time fitness instructor.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs show a heart rate of 102/min and blood pressure of 130/80 mm Hg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
She is alert and cooperative but appears jittery. Her thyroid gland is non-palpable without nodularity or tenderness.

OTHER STUDIES:
A radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan and laboratory studies are performed.
